cards.explanation: The answer is dust. The LORD says, "Go down and sit in the dust, O Virgin Daughter of Babylon." Then He adds, "Sit on the ground without a throne…" She's going from a throne to the ground, friends. That's a long way down.

The answer is False. Babylon is told to "Go down and sit in the dust…" and then the LORD adds, "For you will no longer be called tender or delicate." I'd say a tender, delicate name and a seat in the dust don't go together.
The answer is to grind flour. The LORD says, "Take millstones and grind flour…" I know flour well, friends. I've worn it on my apron for years. Grinding it is a long way from sitting on a throne.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I will take vengeance; I will spare no one." I think this is a heavy line, and it deserves to be heard that way. It comes right after He says her shame will be exposed.
The answer is Israel. The line calls "Our Redeemer" the "Holy One of Israel." It breaks into the message to Babylon. And it says "Our," so whoever speaks it is counting himself in.
The answer is the queen of kingdoms. The LORD says, "For you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms." It's a big, shiny name for an empire, friends. And it's being taken away.

The answer is that Babylon showed them no mercy. The LORD says, "You showed them no mercy…" He adds, "even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke." I think this is one of the heavy parts of the passage. It tells us why her fall is coming.
The answer is False. The LORD says to Babylon, "even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke." She didn't ease up for them. I think that's a heavy detail, and the verse says it plainly.
The answer is queen. Babylon says, "I will be queen forever." Forever is a big word to hand yourself, friends. The LORD has already told her she'll lose the title of queen of kingdoms.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "You did not take these things to heart or consider their outcome." She never stopped to think about where it was all heading. It's like hitting send on a text without rereading it.

The answer is that she says there is none besides her. The LORD quotes her: "I am, and there is none besides me." She's so sure nobody can touch her, friends. She says it again in verse 10, word for word.

The first blank is widow, and the second is children. Babylon says, "I will never be a widow or know the loss of children." The LORD answers in verse 9 that widowhood and the loss of children will both come upon her. I think this is a heavy part of the passage, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is False. The LORD says the losses will come "…in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the potency of your spells." Her spells don't stop a thing, friends. They come in a single day.
The answer is wisdom. The LORD says, "Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray…" What she thought she knew steered her off course. It's like being so sure of your shortcut that you end up lost.
The answer is charm it away. The LORD says, "you will not know how to charm it away." He adds that the calamity is one she'll be "unable to ward off." Her tricks won't work this time, friends.

The answer is that He's daring her to try. In verse 11 the LORD says she'll be "unable to ward off" the calamity. Then in verse 12 He says, "Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror!" I think that's a dare. He's telling her to go ahead and take her best shot.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "let them come forward now and save you…" He's talking about her astrologers, who observe the stars. If they can predict her fate every month, friends, let's see them step up.

The answer is stubble. The LORD says, "Surely they are like stubble; the fire will burn them up." Stubble is the dry leftover that goes up fast. That's a rough comparison for the advisors she trusted.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "There will be no coals to warm them or fire to sit beside." The fire burns them up, and nothing is left to sit beside. It's no campfire, friends.

The answer is that each one strays in his own direction. The LORD says, "…each one strays in his own direction; not one of them can save you." These are the folks she labored and traded with since her youth. So they scatter, each going his own way.
